# Form

> A `<form>` that Slab's controls submit, reset, and validate with — just like native ones.

`<slab-form>` · Form · built on `<form>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/form/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/form.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-form label="Sign up" action="/sign-up" method="post">
  <slab-text-field
    label="Email"
    name="email"
    type="email"
    required
  ></slab-text-field>
  <button>Sign up</button>
</slab-form>
```

A plain `<form>` works with Slab's controls too. Reach for Form when you
want what it adds: a label that makes the form a landmark, and a
`checkValidity()` that doesn't show errors, just like a native one.

## Keyboard

| Key   | What it does                                      |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter | In a field, submits the form, as in a native one. |

## Elements

### `<slab-form>`

Import `slab-elements/form.js` to register it.

A form with no visual styles, around a native `<form>`, so it's submitted, reset and validated the way one is.

The `<form>` is in the light DOM, not the shadow root. A control's form owner is its nearest `<form>` ancestor in its own tree, and that doesn't cross a shadow boundary: a `<form>` in the shadow root with a `<slot>` inside it would own nothing slotted into it, and every control would submit to no form at all. So Form appends a `<form>` as its only child and moves its other children into it, on connect and whenever one is added. The shadow root holds a single `<slot>`, which the `<form>` is slotted into.

Everything else is the `<form>`'s. Slab's controls are form-associated through `ElementInternals`, so they submit, reset, and report their validity to it the way a native `<input>` does, and nothing here walks them. `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`, `requestSubmit()`, `reset()` and `submit()` are the `<form>`'s, and "submit" and "reset" bubble from it through the host.

A native `<form>`'s `checkValidity()` fires "invalid" at each invalid control but shows nothing, and so does this one's: Form marks its own `<form>` while its `checkValidity()` runs, whether it's called on Form or on `form`, and Slab's controls stay out of their error state. Only that `<form>` is marked. `HTMLFormElement.prototype` is left alone, so a consumer's own plain `<form>` gets no such marking, and its `checkValidity()` puts Slab's invalid controls into their error state as `reportValidity()` does.

`label`, when set, names the `<form>`, which is what makes it a form landmark. The `<form>` is reachable as `form` and styled as any light-DOM element is.

#### Attributes

| Name           | Type                          | Default | Description                                                                   |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action`       | `string`                      |         | Where it submits to, as a native form's `action`.                             |
| `autocomplete` | `'on' \| 'off'`               |         | Whether the browser may fill its controls, as a native form's `autocomplete`. |
| `enctype`      | `string`                      |         | How it encodes what it submits, as a native form's `enctype`.                 |
| `label`        | `string`                      |         | Names the form, which makes it a landmark.                                    |
| `method`       | `'get' \| 'post' \| 'dialog'` |         | How it submits, as a native form's `method`.                                  |
| `name`         | `string`                      |         | Its name, as a native form's `name`.                                          |
| `novalidate`   | `boolean`                     | `false` | Submits without checking validity, as a native form's `novalidate`.           |
| `target`       | `string`                      |         | Where the response opens, as a native form's `target`.                        |

#### Properties

| Name                   | Type                         | Description                                  |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `elements` (read-only) | `HTMLFormControlsCollection` | Its controls, as a native form's `elements`. |
| `form` (read-only)     | `HTMLFormElement`            | The native form, in the light DOM            |

#### Methods

| Signature                                              | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                             | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                 |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                            | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does. |
| `requestSubmit(submitter?: HTMLElement \| null): void` | Submits it as a submit button would, checking validity and dispatching "submit", as a native form's `requestSubmit()`.      |
| `reset(): void`                                        | Resets its controls, as a native form's `reset()`.                                                                          |
| `submit(): void`                                       | Submits it without checking validity or dispatching "submit", as a native form's `submit()`.                                |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description         |
| --------- | ------------------- | ------------------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | Moved into the form |
